data.cultural_impact: Sigismund was the name of several kings and rulers in medieval Europe. One notable figure was Sigismund of Luxembourg, who was King of Hungary and Bohemia and played an instrumental role in the election of Friedrich III as Holy Roman Emperor. Another significant Sigismund was Sigismund I the Old, who was the first monarch of the House of Jagiellon in Poland and reigned from 1506 to 1548. The name has a rich historical context, evoking images of powerful and influential leaders.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Sigismund is also associated with several saints. Saint Sigismund of Burgundy was a 6th-century Frankish prince who reigned over Burgundy and is venerated as a patron saint against the plague and as a protector of children. Saint Sigismund of Anhalt was a 12th-century duke of Anhalt and is remembered for his humility, charity, and dedication to the poor and the sick. The name Sigismund brings to mind the triumph of faith and the protecting presence of God in one's life.
